findings.reason: §9's effort estimate and its done-when ("a synthetic flat bundle resolves its catalogue, every signal map and its description store") rest on §2 having generalised resolvers that the code shows are still hardcoded, so the author must name `machine_map.py:136-142` and `load_bundle_descriptor` as §9's edit sites.
findings.text: §9 states "The resolvers §2 generalised read either addressing, chosen by the key present: `MapBundle.machine_map_path` and `signal_map_path`, and store-root resolution." `map_for_shot`/store-root resolution was generalised, but the two path resolvers were not: `packages/imas-alambic/src/imas_alambic/machine_map.py:136` returns `self.root / "machine_maps" / f"{machine}.json"` and `machine_map.py:140` returns `self.root / "maps" / machine / f"{system}.json"`, both hardcoded to the multi-machine layout. A flat bundle (§9: `machine_map.json`, `maps/<ids>.json`) therefore does not resolve at all until those two methods are rewritten to branch on the key present; `load_bundle_descriptor` (`machine_map.py:162`) likewise reads only `machines` and never `machine`. The plan presents work that §9 must actually do as work §2 already did.

findings.reason: the run file is read by the companion plan's §2/§4 and by §6's cross-check, so two spellings produce a reader that opens the wrong path; §8 must name the single owner of the layout and correct `jt60sa-pulse-ids.html:227`, and must say whether the cache root is resolved through `resolve_description_store_root` (extended to be optional) or by a new path.
findings.text: the written-IDS layout is owned in two places with two different spellings. This plan (decision `output-layout`, snapshot plan.html:289-297; §6 plan.html:178 `IMASDB/ids/101154_0.nc`; §5 tree plan.html:173-174; §8 plan.html:186 `<ids root>/<pulse>_<run>.nc`) settles on a flat file `ids/<pulse>_<run>.nc`. The companion plan it defers to records the other spelling: `docs/plans/jt60sa-pulse-ids.html:227` says written IDSs "move from one netCDF per IDS … to one netCDF per run, `ids/<pulse>/<run>.nc`" — a directory per pulse, which is the rejected `ids-pulse-dir-run` option. §8's own text points a reader at "the 2026-10-07 comment on that plan" as the record of this change, but that comment carries the conflicting path. Separately, §8's cache precedence item 4 ("the bundle's store root declared under the role name `eddb_cache`, then a per-user `~/.cache/imas-alambic`") resolves a named bundle store root but names no owner; the existing owner of that mechanism is `resolve_description_store_root` at `machine_map.py:244`, which already walks `discover_bundles()` and refuses on ambiguity but has no optional/absent form the fall-through needs, so §8 would grow a second resolution path beside it.

findings.reason: with every interface family at zero this week, each section that adds surface must account for it in its own text; §8 must name the refusal families it adds (or state they reuse `PulseWriteError`/`MachineMapError` unchanged), and §9 must name the `machine` key as new `bundle.json` vocabulary and what it supersedes.
findings.text: the supplied counts are public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0. §8's interface account ("this adds three environment variables and one command, each against what it retires") accounts for `IMAS_ALAMBIC_HOME`, `IMAS_ALAMBIC_IDS_ROOT`, `IMAS_ALAMBIC_CACHE` and `config`, but does not account for the two refusal behaviours the same section introduces: "A missing setting is refused, naming the variable that sets it" (plan.html:186) and "An existing file is refused unless `--overwrite` is given" (plan.html:186, reinforced by the done-when "A second write without `--overwrite` is refused"). And §9 (plan.html:190) adds the singular `machine` key to `bundle.json` — new accepted schema surface — while asserting "no new vocabulary is added". Neither addition is named against what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be.
